_what_this_is: The lineage of 433-B's AcroForm leaf names against every form already in this engine, judged PER OCCURRENCE.
_the_rule: An inherited leaf name is evidence of nothing. A verdict is per occurrence, never per name. This form is the clearest demonstration of that rule in the tree so far: `p2_t11_13a` and `p2_t15_13b` each MATCH on one occurrence and CONTRADICT on the two beside it, because 433-B's digital-asset table has seven columns where 433-A's has five and the two extra columns reuse the current-value name with a bumped index.
_every_figure_here_is_derived: adapters/pdf/tmp/p46/gen-lineage-433b.mjs, over the five forms' fields files and 433-B's widget geometry. The VERDICTS are authored from the printed column headers of both forms, quoted in each row.
_the_headline: ELEVEN INHERITED NAMES, SEVENTEEN OCCURRENCES, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM IS ON PAGE 3. Page 1 — the page this slice maps — carries not one inherited leaf name, so nothing in this report bears on slice 1 at all. Of the seventeen, 5 match, 10 contradict and 2 are a new question under an inherited name.
_the_registry_intersection_is_empty_and_: Name-lie registries exist on 433-A(OIC) (31 entries) and 433-B(OIC) (37). 433-B shares ZERO leaf names with either. The 11 names it does share are shared with 433-A and 433-F, and neither of those carries a registry. So no entry in any registry in this tree stands on any name this form inherits — not because the names were checked and found clean, but because the two sets never meet. That is a derived zero and it is a different thing from a clean bill of health, which is why it is written out.
_what_this_report_does_not_establish: It says nothing about the 390 leaf names this form does NOT share. Those are judged when their page is read, on the printed page, like everything else.

It does not license reuse. Reuse runs on the SUBJECT axis and is settled in _subjects.cross-form.json: 433-B COINCIDES with 433-B(OIC), with which it shares no leaf name at all, and is MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with 433-A and 433-F, with which it shares all eleven. The two axes point opposite ways on this form, which is the sharpest available illustration that leaf-name overlap is not the reuse axis.
The [B-03] finding in the Line19c row is recorded, not resolved: it is a page-3 name lie and page 3 is not in this slice.
